requirements.quote:
The
   basic data block size is one byte (i.e., 8 bits).
requirements.condition: data is represented using the TLS presentation language
requirements.required_behavior: use an 8-bit byte as the basic data block
requirements.forbidden_behavior: use a basic data block with a size other than 8 bits
requirements.why_checkable: Serialized field widths and parser byte consumption can be measured.

requirements.quote:
Multiple-byte data
   items are concatenations of bytes, from left to right, from top to
   bottom.  From the byte stream, a multi-byte item (a numeric in the
   following example) is formed (using C notation) by:

      value = (byte[0] << 8*(n-1)) | (byte[1] << 8*(n-2)) |
              ... | byte[n-1];

   This byte ordering for multi-byte values is the commonplace network
   byte order or big-endian format.
requirements.condition: a data item occupies multiple bytes
requirements.required_behavior: encode and decode the item in network byte order with the leftmost byte as the most significant byte
requirements.forbidden_behavior: interpret a multi-byte item in little-endian or reversed byte order
requirements.why_checkable: Known multi-byte values have deterministic serialized byte sequences.
